title: Legacy Application Migration to Compute Engine
business: Enterprises maintaining monolithic legacy applications that require specific OS configurations and persistent storage environments.
problem: High operational overhead and lack of flexibility when managing on-premises hardware for legacy applications that cannot be easily containerized.
solution: Compute Engine provides customizable virtual machines that allow businesses to lift and shift legacy workloads into a managed cloud environment, retaining full control over the OS and network stack while gaining infrastructure scalability.
steps: Assess the legacy application requirements including CPU, RAM, and disk storage needs.
Create a custom machine image or select a pre-configured OS image within Compute Engine.
Configure Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) settings to ensure secure network connectivity.
Deploy the virtual machine instance and attach persistent disks for data storage.
Verify application functionality and performance within the new virtualized environment.
outcome: Improved infrastructure agility and reduced maintenance burden by offloading hardware lifecycle management to Google Cloud.
limitation: Compute Engine requires manual management of the guest operating system, including patching and security updates, which can be checked by monitoring OS-level logs and security compliance reports.
